subject.title: [Architecture] Standardize audio/video asset pipeline across TTS and media generation skills

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a shared core asset lifecycle contract across TTS, image generation, and video generation, or keep asset handling with the current feature owners until a concrete cross-tool invariant is demonstrated?
rationale: The report requests a new foundational abstraction and automatic retention policy, but does not establish the intended ownership boundary, persistence model, migration behavior, or the failure that current paths cannot solve.

options.title: Require a scoped design first
options.body: Document concrete duplicated invariants, lifecycle ownership, retention semantics, and upgrade effects before accepting any cross-tool refactor.

options.title: Keep feature-owned handling
options.body: Retain the existing owner-specific media paths and address future defects at the responsible TTS, image, or video surface.

options.title: Sponsor a shared media-core contract
options.body: Approve a focused design and implementation plan for a common asset lifecycle API with explicit compatibility and migration proof.

recommendation.title: Require a scoped design first
recommendation.body: Document concrete duplicated invariants, lifecycle ownership, retention semantics, and upgrade effects before accepting any cross-tool refactor.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent TTS managed-outbound-media work is the closest identified history signal for the proposed lifecycle boundary.
